conviction_note: The print turns on one decision: does the company raise its full-year plan at H1? Three primary facts lean yes. Q1 ordinary profit was already 33.8% of the FY plan against a 5-year average of 19.2%. The April tanshin says the -24% OP guide is a Middle East risk haircut taken off an underlying view of profit flat with last year. And the company raised at H1 in 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2025. Against that, it held at Q1 despite the same progress, and the stock fell 10.4% on that hold. The upgrade is also flagged on two kabutan lists, and margin longs are crowded at 7.9x. So p_up is 62 on an abs move of 7.5 (raised from the 5.15 proxy because a forecast decision is likely), giving +1.8. The findings sum to +2.0; the two numbers agree.

positioning_check: JPX disclosed short register: 0.0%, no position at or above 0.5%, unchanged (as of 2026-10-26, https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html, via baseline). findings.finding: Three primary facts point to an upward FY revision with the H1 release. Q1 FY3/27 ordinary profit was 3,142m, 33.8% of the 9,300m plan against a 5-year Q1 average of 19.2%; Q1 OP was 2,923m, +86% y/y. The April tanshin says the guide was cut from an initial view of profit 'about the same as last year' (FY3/26 OP 11,615m) purely as a Middle East buffer. And the company raised its full-year ordinary forecast at or before H1 in 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raise at Q1 FY3/26 (2025-07-28, ordinary +19%): +13.5% next day. Second raise at H1 FY3/26 (2025-10-28): +14.7% (3,035 to 3,480 close). No raise at Q1 FY3/27 despite 33.8% progress (2026-07-28): -10.4% (3,835 to 3,435). The tape is in the baseline history and Yahoo daily bars; the revision dates are from kabutan.
findings.why_not_priced: The progress rate is public, and kabutan has flagged the name for an upgrade twice (10/18 and 10/25), so 'a revision' is partly expected. Two things are not priced. (1) Its size: the April tanshin shows the plan embeds a discretionary Middle East haircut of roughly 2.8bn yen of OP, and Q1 alone ran 1.35bn ahead of last year. (2) The decision itself: the company held at Q1, and the market sold that 10.4%. The stock is at 3,750, below the 3,880 it held into the Q1 print. It still trades at 7.2x the cut guide with no analyst consensus, and a fully priced raise would have taken it back above the pre-Q1 level. Last year's two raises each added 13-15% on the day despite similar run-ins, so on this thinly covered name the decision is not front-run.
findings.independence: Kabutan's revision history and progress table (https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=7102) give the Q1 progress and the 21/10, 22/10, 23/10 and 25/10 revisions independently of the tanshin. The kabutan 10/25 upward-revision list (https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=7102&b=n202610250063) computes 33.8% against 19.2% and counts 3 raises in 5 years. The Q1 explanation deck (https://www.n-sharyo.co.jp/finance/198R8-qtr1setumei.pdf) attributes the Q1 gain to rail product mix plus cost reduction and confirms the plan was unchanged. That is three documents, all read from public material, and they share the underlying progress number.

findings.finding: The dividend plan pays out only 9.6% of guided EPS (50 yen on 519.8). At the FY3/26 print the company raised the year-end dividend by 5 yen 'reflecting results stronger than assumed', so a profit raise at H1 could carry a dividend raise in the same batch.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 5-yen year-end raise came with the FY3/26 results (2026-04-24) alongside a -22% ordinary guide. The 4/24 close was 3,505 (3,615 prior). The baseline's estimated reaction is +5.25% at 2026-04-28, so the dividend effect cannot be separated from the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody publishes a dividend expectation for this name: there is no consensus and no 四季報 access. The company's habit is to raise at the full-year print, not at H1, so the market would not be paying for an H1 raise. This is an inference, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: None from a different source. It shares the tanshin with finding 1 and is conditional on the same revision.

findings.finding: Leveraged retail is crowded long into the print. The margin long balance rose from 72.7k shares (10/02) to 85.4k (10/23), a 7.91x ratio against 10.8k short, with no disclosed short on the JPX register. A hold or a token raise therefore has forced sellers, as the -10.4% after the Q1 hold showed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY3/27 (2026-07-28): a run-in to 3,880, no raise, then -10.4% and a further -2.3% the next session on 200k shares, about 4-5x normal volume.
findings.why_not_priced: The margin balance is public, and the baseline's priced_lean_pct already carries -0.45 for it. What it adds here is the asymmetry: the downside branch of finding 1 is deeper than the upside because retail longs who bought the kabutan upgrade lists have to exit on a hold. That is why this is sized below the baseline component rather than on top of it.
findings.independence: The baseline's margin_ratio (7.91, a broker scrape) is the same number. There is no independent second source.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision expected? Yes, likely upward: Q1 progress is 33.8% against a 19.2% 5-year average, the guide carries an explicit Middle East buffer, and the company revised at H1 in 4 of the last 5 years. Returns? A possible dividend raise (payout 9.6%), but the habit is to raise at FY. New-year guide? Not applicable at H1. Quarter against its own 進捗率? Q1 alone was 33.8% of the FY plan; H1 FY3/26 was 35.6% of that year's actual, and FY3/25 was 46.9%.

baseline_tension: The finding is positive and cuts against the baseline lean (-0.50, from the margin overhang) but not against the run-up (+0.94% over 20 days, +3.5% over 5). The strongest negative the release could carry is a second hold of the plan citing Middle East uncertainty, as at Q1. I looked for it, and that is why the guidance finding's range runs to -8 and why p_up stops at 62.
lessons_applied: nothing changed. Rule 1 (a negative on a public series goes toward 50) does not apply: the guidance finding is positive and rests on a decision the release adds, not on a visible miss. Rule 2 (check a negative tilt) does not apply: one small negative against two positives. Open question 4 (run-in as a short signal) agrees with not sizing the 5-day run-in as a negative, which the draft already did not do.
